title: Open graph projections and division charts for a strict law
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset Y$ in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for every $s\in S$. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, modulo agreement on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Smoothness and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A strict birational law on a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $Y$ with nonempty fibres is an associative $S$-rational map $m:Y\times_SY\dashrightarrow Y$ for which there are opens $D,V,W\subset Y\times_SY$, each dense in every fibre of both projections to $Y$, such that $m$ is defined on $D$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$, $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$ and $D\simeq W$, respectively. Let $Y$ carry such a strict law $m$, represented on a strictness domain $D$. Let $\Gamma\subset Y\times_SY\times_SY$ be the schematic closure of its graph $\{(x,y,m(x,y)):(x,y)\in D\}$, where schematic closure means the smallest closed subscheme containing this graph. For $1\leq i<j\leq3$ let $q_{ij}:\Gamma\to Y\times_SY$ be the indicated coordinate projection. Each $q_{ij}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and its image is dense in every fibre of both projections $Y\times_SY\to Y$. The image of $q_{12}$ is the maximal domain of $m$. The formula $d=q_2\circ q_{13}^{-1}$, with $q_2:\Gamma\to Y$ the second coordinate, defines a rational left-division map $d:Y\times_SY\dashrightarrow Y$, with maximal domain $q_{13}(\Gamma)$, such that $m(x,d(x,z))=z$ there. Both $m(x,y)$ and $d(x,z)$, considered as rational maps in either one variable with the other fixed at any scheme point, are birational maps between dense opens of the corresponding fibre; their domains and images remain dense after residue-field extension. For the translations of [lem-sfb-strict-law-translation-embedding], every $T$-valued point $(a,b,c)$ of $\Gamma$ satisfies $\tau_a\circ\tau_b=\tau_c$, in particular $\tau_{d(a,c)}=\tau_a^{-1}\circ\tau_c$ wherever $d(a,c)$ is defined.

source.place: 5.3 Lemmas 2-3 and the paragraph following Lemma 3, printed pp.120-121 (PDF pp.126-127); primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf, local PDF WANTED

proof.text: Write $P=Y\times_SY$, and let $G\subset Y^3$ be the graph over $D$. The projection $Y^n\to Y^{n-1}$ is a base change of $Y\to S$, hence smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Normality ascends along each such smooth morphism [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent], starting with the normal scheme $S$. Thus $P$ and $Y^3$ are normal and reduced. They are of finite type over $S$ by base change and composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and Noetherian: on the finite affine covers supplied by finite type, the coordinate rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The graph is closed over $D$ by separatedness of $Y$ (it is the pullback of its diagonal), hence $G=\Gamma\cap(D\times_SY)$ as schemes. By the kernel-ideal description of schematic closure [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], $G$ is schematically dense in $\Gamma$. Moreover $\Gamma$ is reduced: a nilpotent local section restricts to zero on the reduced scheme $G\simeq D$, and schematic density makes that section zero. The closed subscheme $\Gamma$ is of finite type over $S$: affine-locally its ring is a quotient of a finite-type algebra, still generated by the images of the same generators.

source.place: 5.3 Lemmas 2-3; 2.3/9 for normality of smooth schemes over a normal base

proof.text: In $Y^4$ let $R$ be the open where $(y,w),(z,w),(x,m(y,w))$ belong to $D$. Its fibre over any point $(x,y,z)$ of $Y^3$ is dense in the corresponding $w$-fibre. Indeed, after passing to its residue field, $w\mapsto m(y,w)$ identifies the dense open $D_y$ with the dense open $V_y$. The inverse image of the dense open $D_x$ therefore cuts out a dense open of $D_y$, and intersecting with $D_z$ stays dense. Here a finite intersection of dense opens is dense, without an irreducibility assumption. The strict charts and all their fibre-density assertions persist under the needed residue-field extensions by [lem-sfb-strict-law-base-change]. The same reasoning for any point after any $T\to Y^3$ proves that the inverse image $R_T\subset Y_T$ is $T$-dense. In particular this holds for $T=\Gamma$ and for every test scheme mapping to $\Gamma$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 1, printed p.120 (PDF p.126): the generic fourth-variable domain

proof.text: On $G\times_SY$, the two morphisms $m(x,m(y,w))$ and $m(z,w)$ agree wherever $R$ is defined. To justify agreement on that entire open, associativity first gives agreement on a dense common open of $Y^3$ with coordinates $(x,y,w)$; on the common domain of the two iterates, the equalizer is closed by separatedness. That common domain is reduced by step 1, so a dense open is schematically dense by [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic], and the equalizer is the whole domain. On $G$ one has $z=m(x,y)$, giving the asserted equality. The projection $\Gamma\times_SY\to\Gamma$ is flat: it is the base change of the smooth morphism $Y\to S$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change, lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Therefore [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] makes $G\times_SY$ schematically dense in $\Gamma\times_SY$. Restrict this density to the open $R\cap(\Gamma\times_SY)$; the kernel sheaf remains zero on restriction. Its two morphisms to the separated scheme $Y$ have a closed equalizer. The ideal of that equalizer restricts to zero on the schematically dense open coming from $G$, so it is zero. Consequently $m(x,m(y,w))=m(z,w)$ holds on all of $R\cap(\Gamma\times_SY)$, including its nilpotent test points.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 2 proof: schematic density after flat pullback and the closed equalizer

proof.text: For $(a,b,c)\in\Gamma(T)$, pull the equality of step 3 back along $(a,b,c,\mathrm{id}):Y_T\to\Gamma\times_SY$. Its domain is $T$-dense by step 2. On it the two sides represent $\tau_a\circ\tau_b$ and $\tau_c$ respectively, so these birational maps are equal. This proves the claimed identity even for nonreduced $T$; no assertion of schematic density after the possibly nonflat map $T\to\Gamma$ was used. Now two triples with the same first and second coordinates have the same third coordinate by injectivity in [lem-sfb-strict-law-translation-embedding]. The same applies to coordinates $(1,3)$ or $(2,3)$, since cancellation in the group $B_Y(T)$ recovers the missing translation. Thus all three $q_{ij}$ are monomorphisms on every functor of points.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 2 conclusion and Lemma 3, first paragraph

proof.text: The maps $q_{ij}$ are of finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], since $\Gamma\to S$ is of finite type and $P\to S$ is separated: its diagonal is the intersection of the inverse images of the two closed diagonals of $Y$ under the coordinate-pair projections. Thus it is a closed immersion, locally cut out by the sum of the two pulled-back ideals. Write $\sigma(W)=\{(y,u):(u,y)\in W\}$ for the image of $W$ under the factor swap of $P$; it is dense in every fibre of both projections because $W$ is. For $q_{12},q_{13},q_{23}$ the open graph $G$ maps isomorphically onto $D$, $V$ and $\sigma(W)$, respectively, by the given strictness charts: $q_{23}$ sends $(x,y,m(x,y))$ to $(y,m(x,y))$, the swap of the $W$-chart point $(m(x,y),y)$. It is the entire inverse image of that open: a monomorphism with a section over an open is an isomorphism there, since the two composites are forced to be identities by cancellation. The opens $D,V,\sigma(W)$ are dense in $P$ (their density in every projection fibre implies density globally), and $G$ is dense in the reduced scheme $\Gamma$ by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-quasifinite-normal-dense-open-immersion] to each $q_{ij}$, with normal Noetherian target $P$. Every hypothesis has now been verified. Hence all $q_{ij}$ are open immersions. Their images contain $D,V,\sigma(W)$, respectively, so they remain dense in every fibre of both projections of $P$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 3 proof: Zariski Main and density of the strictness charts

proof.text: Let $M=q_{12}(\Gamma)$ and $L=q_{13}(\Gamma)$. The inverses to the open immersions give morphisms $q_3q_{12}^{-1}:M\to Y$ and $q_2q_{13}^{-1}:L\to Y$. They extend the multiplication and left-division charts on $D$ and $V$. To check maximality, let $r:E\to Y$ be any representative of multiplication. The morphism $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y,r(x,y))$ on $E$ factors through the closed subscheme $\Gamma$: on the dense open $E\cap D$ it does so, since two representatives agree as morphisms there by the reduced closed-equalizer argument of step 3. Since $E$ is reduced and Noetherian, [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] makes that dense open schematically dense in $E$; the pullback of the ideal of $\Gamma$ must vanish. This factorization shows $E\subset M$. For any representative $r:E\to Y$ of division, use instead $(x,z)\mapsto(x,r(x,z),z)$ and the dense open $E\cap V$ to obtain $E\subset L$. Thus $M,L$ are precisely the maximal domains. On $L$, the triple $q_{13}^{-1}(x,z)=(x,d(x,z),z)$ also maps into $M$ under $q_{12}$, proving $m(x,d(x,z))=z$ everywhere on $L$.

source.place: 5.3 paragraph following Lemma 3, printed p.121: division and domains of definition

proof.text: Fixing the first coordinate, the restrictions of $q_{12}$ and $q_{13}$ to the same fibre of $\Gamma\to Y$ identify dense opens of the two copies of the remaining $Y$-fibre. Their composite is multiplication in the second variable, and its inverse is division in the second variable. Fixing the second coordinate instead, $q_{12}$ and $q_{23}$ give multiplication in the first variable. Finally fix the third coordinate: $q_{13}$ and $q_{23}$ identify the $x$- and $y$-opens, giving division in the first variable. All domains and images here are dense by step 5. For a further residue-field extension, an open immersion and its inverse base change to inverse isomorphisms; density persists by the general fibrewise-open density assertion of [lem-sfb-strict-law-base-change]. This verifies birationality in each of the four cases with all residue-field extensions. Lastly step 4 applied to $(a,d(a,c),c)$ gives $\tau_a\tau_{d(a,c)}=\tau_c$; multiply on the left by $\tau_a^{-1}$ in $B_Y(T)$ to obtain the required division identity.
